1.evidence_source: Title: "Body Mass Index and Weight Loss Efforts in Middle-Aged Saudi Women: The Mediating Role of Body Appreciation"
1._section_summary: This section shows the paper title and author: it investigates BMI and weight-loss efforts among middle-aged Saudi women and examines body appreciation as a mediator. The text does not provide sample sizes, methods, measures, or statistical results, nor does it label any studies explicitly (no 'Study 1' etc.).

2.evidence_source: Abstract: 'Body Appreciation (BA) ... Little is known about BA among Saudi middle-aged women ... recruited from all primary health centers in Hofuf city.'
2._section_summary: This abstract reports a single cross-sectional study of 326 middle-aged Saudi women recruited from primary health centers in Hofuf city, examining body appreciation (BA), BMI, and weight-loss (WL) efforts. Mean age was 49.14 years and mean BMI 29.64 kg/m2; 78.5% had attempted weight loss and BA fully mediated the relationship between BMI and WL. The abstract does not report the specific BA instrument (BAS/BAS-2), whether BMI was measured or self-reported, racial/ethnic composition, or numeric correlation coefficients.

3.evidence_source: Saudi Arabia has one of the highest prevalence rates of obesity/ overweight worldwide, in that seven out of 10 people are overweight or obese; especially among women.
3._section_summary: This introduction reviews obesity and body image issues in middle-aged women, highlights high obesity prevalence in Saudi Arabia, and notes limited research on body appreciation (BA) in middle-aged Saudi women. It states the current study's aims to assess BA, weight status, and weight-loss efforts and to test whether BA mediates the association between BMI-based weight status and weight-loss efforts. No study numbering or sample details are provided in the text.

4.evidence_source: All the primary health centeres (nine) in Hofuf city, Saudi Arabia, were included in the study.
4._section_summary: This Methods section describes a single cross-sectional, face-to-face interview study conducted over October–December 2017 using convenience sampling at nine primary health centers in Hofuf city, Saudi Arabia. The target (required) sample size was 207 women aged 45–65 years, data were collected via trained nutritionists who conducted interviews and performed anthropometric measurements; no results (e.g., mean age, BMI, racial composition, or body appreciation measures) are reported in this section.

5.evidence_source: A total of 326 middle-aged Saudi women were enrolled in this  study.
5._section_summary: Study X enrolled 326 middle-aged Saudi women (mean age 49.14 years). Mean BMI was 29.64 kg/m2 and mean body appreciation (BA) was 3.92; BA correlated negatively with BMI (r=-0.237, p<0.01). Mediation analyses indicated BA fully mediated the relationship between BMI and weight loss (WL).

6.evidence_source: A total of 326 middle-aged Saudi women were enrolled in this study.

4.evidence_source: Women were also asked on separate question about their reason for weight loss with six options (to look better, for easier movement, to be healthier, to be able to wear a wider range of clothes, because of family or friends' comments, and to be sexier) to know more about the main reason that can influence women to lose weight.

Correlation analysis was used to examine univariate relationships among BMI, body appreciation (BA), and weight loss (WL), and mediation was tested using PROCESS Model 4 (1000 bias-corrected bootstrap samples) with BMI as X, BA as M, and WL as Y; significance was set at p < .05.
